title: Free GIZ Data Governance Certificate Courses for African Policymakers and Professionals: Build Skills in Africa’s Data Economy
summary: GIZ Data Governance offers specialised online certificate courses through the atingi digital learning platform , providing learners and professionals with an opportunity to strengthen essential skills in data governance, Africa’s data economy, digital policy, cross-border data flows, data localisation, trust, accountability and responsible data value creation. The courses are provided by GIZ 1740 DataCipation and are particularly relevant to policymakers, regulators, public-sector professionals, IT representatives supporting policy teams, non-technical practitioners and learners interested in building careers in African data governance and digital policy. Three courses highlighted under the From Policy to Data Value Creation learning offering include: The African Data Economy in the Global Context Guardians of Trust Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows Each course has an estimated learning duration of approximately 1.5 hours and provides a certificate after assessment . The courses form part of the broader From Policy to Data Value Creation learning offering and are particularly relevant for people working or seeking to work at the intersection of data, governance, regulation, digital transformation and public policy in Africa. About the GIZ Data Governance Courses on atingi Data has become an increasingly important resource for governments, businesses, researchers, development organisations and communities. However, creating value from data involves much more than simply collecting information. Questions surrounding who can access data, where information can be stored, how it can move across borders, which safeguards should apply, how institutions cooperate, and how citizens and stakeholders can participate in governance decisions have become central to Africa s digital development. These GIZ DataCipation courses introduce learners to different dimensions of those challenges. Rather than treating data governance as an exclusively technical subject, the courses examine its broader societal, regulatory, institutional and economic dimensions . This makes the learning opportunity particularly relevant to policymakers and other professionals who may not be data scientists or software engineers but whose work involves decisions about digital policy, governance, regulation, institutional coordination or public-sector transformation. The training also demonstrates how African countries and institutions can play an active role in shaping the continent s data agenda instead of simply adapting to global data systems and standards created elsewhere. Why Africa s Data Economy Matters Africa s digital transformation is generating growing quantities of data across governments, businesses, financial systems, telecommunications networks, healthcare systems, agriculture, education, infrastructure and other sectors. However, data only produces meaningful value when appropriate systems allow it to be accessed, shared, combined and reused responsibly. This creates several important policy questions. For example: How should data move between institutions within the same country? Under what circumstances should data be allowed to move across national borders? What safeguards should exist when data is shared? How can governments preserve sovereignty while participating in regional and global data ecosystems? How can African countries cooperate on common data-governance principles? How can institutions build public trust in the way data is collected and used? How can stakeholders participate meaningfully in data-governance processes? What role should accountability play when data is exchanged? How can combining local and regional datasets generate additional economic or public value? The three courses approach these issues from complementary perspectives. Course 1: The African Data Economy in the Global Context The African Data Economy in the Global Context examines how Africa s data economy connects local circumstances with regional and global data systems. The course emphasises the importance of effective data governance as part of sustainable development and explores Africa s position within the wider global data ecosystem. One of its central ideas is that Africa should not be viewed only as a participant in international data systems. African governments, institutions and stakeholders can also actively shape the rules, principles and priorities governing the continent s data future. What Does The African Data Economy in the Global Context Cover? Participants explore the relationship between local, continental and global data systems while considering why cooperation between countries matters. The course uses real-world cases and African policy frameworks to demonstrate how data governance operates in practice. Particular attention is given to: Africa s continental data agenda; regional and international data systems; cross-border data flows; cooperation between countries and institutions; African data-governance frameworks; principles supporting trusted data sharing; the creation of public value from data; economic value creation; local and regional data integration; and Africa s ability to shape its own data agenda. The programme therefore gives participants a wider perspective on data governance beyond the policies of an individual institution or country. Learning Outcomes for The African Data Economy in the Global Context By completing the course, learners should be able to: Describe the main idea behind Africa s continental data agenda and explain why cooperation surrounding data across national borders is important. Identify important African data-governance frameworks and understand their basic purposes. Explain how combining local and regional data can create value , including through examples drawn from Gabon and Kenya. Recognise governance principles that support trusted cross-border data sharing. These outcomes can be particularly valuable to professionals whose work increasingly requires them to understand how domestic policy interacts with continental and international digital developments. How Long Does The African Data Economy in the Global Context Course Take? The estimated duration is: 1.5 hours This relatively short format makes the course accessible to working professionals who may want to strengthen their understanding of the subject without committing to a lengthy academic programme. Certificate for The African Data Economy in the Global Context A certificate is available after assessment . Participants should therefore expect to complete the required assessment associated with the course to obtain certification. Publication Date The supplied course information states that The African Data Economy in the Global Context was published on 12 March 2026 . APPLY NOW Course 2: Guardians of Trust The second course, Guardians of Trust , turns attention toward participation, legitimacy, accountability and stakeholder cooperation in data governance. Effective data governance cannot depend entirely on technical rules or regulations. Institutions also need the confidence and participation of the people and organisations affected by decisions about data. The course consequently explores how participatory approaches to data governance can strengthen trust, legitimacy and accountability across Africa s evolving digital environment . What Does Guardians of Trust Cover? Using African cases and governance practices, learners examine how engagement and cooperation can contribute to more effective and resilient data-governance systems. The programme focuses particularly on the importance of: stakeholder engagement; participatory data governance; inclusive governance mechanisms; accountability; legitimacy; public trust; institutional cooperation; multi-stakeholder approaches; public-interest considerations; innovation; and resilient data-governance systems. The course highlights an important tension in contemporary digital governance: institutions need governance arrangements capable of protecting the public interest while still allowing innovation and responsible data use to develop. Collaboration is presented as an important part of achieving that balance. Why Participatory Data Governance Is Important Data-governance decisions can affect many different groups. Government departments, regulators, businesses, technology providers, civil society organisations, researchers and members of the public may have different priorities and concerns. A governance system that does not sufficiently account for relevant stakeholders can encounter challenges surrounding legitimacy, public confidence and implementation. Participatory approaches can help institutions better understand those competing interests and create governance mechanisms that are more inclusive and accountable. For policymakers and regulators, this means that successful data governance is not simply about writing rules. It can also involve creating mechanisms through which stakeholders can contribute, institutions can cooperate and decision-makers can remain accountable. Guardians of Trust Learning Outcomes By the end of the course, participants should be able to: Understand the main idea behind Africa s continental data agenda and why cooperation on data across borders matters. Identify important African data-governance frameworks and understand their fundamental purposes. Explore how combining local and regional information can generate value, including through examples involving Kenya and Gabon . Recognise governance principles supporting trusted data sharing between countries . These learning outcomes provide participants with both policy context and practical examples for understanding the governance structures surrounding Africa s developing data economy. How Long Is the Guardians of Trust Course? The stated course duration is: 1.5 hours Does Guardians of Trust Provide a Certificate? Yes. According to the supplied course information, participants can receive a certificate after assessment . Learners seeking certification should therefore ensure they complete the required assessment rather than only reviewing the learning materials. Guardians of Trust Publication Date The supplied information gives the publication date as: 12 April 2026 APPLY NOW Course 3: Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows The third course is titled Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows . This course concentrates specifically on the journey that data takes through different systems and examines where value can be created as information moves locally and internationally. It explores data flows beginning within individual countries and continuing to exchanges taking place across national and regional borders. A major theme of the course is that governance matters at every stage of this process . Understanding Data Localisation and Cross-Border Data Flows Data does not automatically generate value simply because it exists. How information is governed can influence: who can access it; how it can be reused; whether institutions can share it; where it can move; what safeguards apply; who is accountable for its use; and whether different systems and institutions can cooperate effectively. The course examines how decisions made throughout the data lifecycle influence access, reuse and value creation. It also explores the relationship between strong domestic data governance and the ability of countries to participate effectively in trusted cross-border data exchanges. Local Data Governance as the Foundation for Wider Data Sharing One of the important ideas addressed by the course is that effective international or regional data sharing depends partly on what happens at the local level. Strong local data governance can provide a foundation for trusted and scalable data use. Several factors can influence whether data moves effectively within a country, including: governance structures; standards; institutional coordination; accountability; appropriate safeguards; clarity of purpose; and alignment between relevant institutions and frameworks. If these underlying conditions are weak, scaling data sharing across borders can become considerably more complicated. Cross-Border Data Flows Are Governed Pathways The course also challenges the idea that cross-border data flows should be understood as purely automatic or technical processes. Instead, Africa s approach can involve treating them as governed pathways . For data to move responsibly across borders, appropriate conditions may need to exist. These include: Purpose – There should be clarity regarding why information is being shared and what the exchange is intended to achieve. Safeguards – Appropriate protections need to accompany the movement and use of data. Accountability – Institutions and actors involved in data exchanges need appropriate responsibilities and accountability mechanisms. Alignment – Policies, systems or institutional approaches may require sufficient alignment to facilitate responsible cooperation. Regional coordination – Cross-border exchanges can require cooperation that extends beyond individual national institutions. The course therefore places value creation alongside other important considerations such as trust and sovereignty . Learning Outcomes for Unleashing Data Value After completing Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows , learners should be able to: Understand the data lifecycle and identify where value can be created as data moves through different systems. Identify factors enabling or constraining local data flows , including governance, standards and institutional coordination. Analyse the relationship between domestic data governance and cross-border data sharing. Evaluate the conditions necessary for responsible and trusted cross-border data flows , including purpose, safeguards, accountability and alignment. These competencies are particularly useful for professionals who need to understand not only whether data can be shared but also the governance conditions under which such sharing can take place responsibly. Course Duration and Certification The stated duration for Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows is: 1.5 hours Participants can also obtain a certificate after assessment . APPLY NOW Who Are These GIZ Data Governance Courses Designed For? Across the three courses, the intended audience is centred on professionals working at the intersection of data and governance across Africa . The programmes are particularly relevant to entry- and mid-level professionals , including IT representatives whose work supports policy teams. The courses may be especially useful for: Policymakers dealing with digital transformation, data or technology policy; Government regulators; Public-sector professionals; IT representatives supporting policy and governance teams; Professionals who already possess foundational knowledge of data governance and want greater regional or international context; Non-technical professionals who need to understand the societal implications of data; Practitioners interested in regulatory aspects of data governance; Professionals interested in institutional approaches to data; Learners considering careers in African data governance; and People interested in pursuing careers related to digital policy. Importantly, these courses are not presented as highly technical programmes intended exclusively for programmers, data scientists or engineers. Their focus extends into policy, institutions, governance, regulation and society, making them potentially valuable for professionals whose responsibilities involve making or supporting decisions about data rather than building the underlying technology. What Skills and Knowledge Can Participants Develop? Taken together, the three courses provide learners with an opportunity to build a broader understanding of Africa s data-governance environment. Participants can explore several interconnected areas. 1. Africa s Continental Data Agenda Learners can develop a clearer understanding of Africa s emerging continental approach to data and why regional cooperation is becoming increasingly important. 2. African Data-Governance Frameworks The courses introduce participants to important frameworks and help them understand their basic purposes within the wider African data ecosystem. 3. Cross-Border Data Cooperation Participants explore why information may need to move between countries and what governance principles can make those exchanges more responsible and trustworthy. 4. Data Value Creation The courses examine how information can generate economic and public value, particularly when local and regional data can be combined or responsibly reused. 5. Trust and Accountability Participants can strengthen their understanding of why trust, institutional accountability and legitimacy are fundamental components of sustainable data governance. 6. Stakeholder Participation Learners examine how inclusive and multi-stakeholder mechanisms can improve governance and help balance innovation with the public interest. 7. Data Localisation Participants can explore local data flows and the governance conditions affecting how information is accessed, used and exchanged within countries. 8. Data Lifecycle Governance The training considers how decisions made throughout the lifecycle of data can affect access, reuse, sharing and ultimately the value generated from information. 9. Data Sovereignty The programmes place cross-border cooperation within the wider discussion about sovereignty, demonstrating that international data sharing and national interests need to be considered together. Kenya and Gabon as Practical African Examples The supplied course descriptions specifically reference examples involving Kenya and Gabon . These examples are used to help participants understand how combining local and regional data can create value. This practical approach is important because data governance can otherwise appear highly abstract. By examining African cases, participants can connect concepts such as regional data cooperation, trusted sharing and value creation with situations grounded in the continent s own institutional and policy environment. Course Provider: GIZ 1740 DataCipation The provider listed for the courses is GIZ 1740 DataCipation . The course pages also identify Germany s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) . The courses are delivered through atingi , the digital learning platform through which learners can access course materials and enrol in the programmes. Certification After Assessment A significant feature of all three courses is the availability of a certificate after assessment . The supplied information does not state that certificates are awarded merely for opening or viewing the courses. Learners should therefore complete the relevant course requirements and assessment to qualify for the certificate. For professionals developing careers in data governance, public policy or digital transformation, certificates can also provide evidence of continued professional learning in specialised subject areas. How Much Time Is Required? Each of the three highlighted courses has an estimated duration of approximately 1.5 hours . Completing all three would therefore represent approximately 4.5 hours of stated course duration , although the actual amount of time an individual learner spends may vary depending on their learning pace and assessment requirements. The relatively short format could make the courses particularly convenient for busy public-sector professionals and policymakers. How to Enrol in the Courses The course pages indicate that people viewing the programmes as guests need to enrol before taking the courses . The general process is: Visit the relevant course page on the atingi platform. Select the option to enrol. Existing atingi users should log in to their accounts where required. People who do not already have an account will need to register on the platform. Enrol in the selected course. Work through the course materials. Complete the required assessment. Meet the applicable requirements to obtain the course certificate. Learners interested in the wider subject area should also explore the From Policy to Data Value Creation learning offering, under which these courses are listed. Is There an Application Deadline? No enrolment or application deadline is stated in the supplied course information. Prospective learners should therefore avoid assuming that a particular closing date applies unless one is displayed during the enrolment process or subsequently announced by the course provider. The first course, The African Data Economy in the Global Context , has a stated publication date of 12 March 2026 , while Guardians of Trust has a stated publication date of 12 April 2026 . No publication date was included in the supplied information for Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows . Course Licensing and Reuse of Materials The supplied information states that the course materials are licensed under CC BY-SA unless stated differently within the course . Learners or organisations interested in reusing course materials should therefore pay attention to the specific licensing information and any exceptions displayed within individual course resources. Disclosure of Artificial Intelligence Use in Course Development The course provider also includes a disclosure explaining how artificial intelligence was incorporated into the content-development process. According to the disclosure, the written course materials were created by Akryl Digital Agency using trusted sources, including official partner sources and other materials supplied by stakeholders. The disclosure states that ChatGPT 5.2 was subsequently used to reword and summarise material while seeking to preserve factual accuracy and make the content more appropriate for e-learning. AI was also used to support activities such as: Generating and reflecting on ideas; Drafting module structures; and Refining didactic methods. The stated period during which the tool was used was October 2025 to February 2026 . Questions concerning the role of AI in developing the materials can be directed to the course-design contact provided by the publisher at design@akryl.consulting . Course Contact Information The course contact listed across the supplied course information is: Lorretta Kade Email: lorretta.kade@giz.de Prospective learners with questions that are not addressed on the course platform may use the listed contact details to seek additional information from the provider. Why These Courses May Be Valuable for African Digital Policy Professionals Africa s digital transformation increasingly requires professionals who can understand technology through the lens of governance, institutions, regulation and public value. Data-sharing systems can create significant opportunities, but those opportunities also introduce questions surrounding responsibility, sovereignty, accountability, safeguards and trust. The three GIZ DataCipation courses approach these challenges from interconnected perspectives. The African Data Economy in the Global Context helps participants understand Africa s position within wider regional and global data ecosystems. Guardians of Trust highlights the human and institutional dimensions of governance, particularly participation, legitimacy, accountability and stakeholder cooperation. Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows examines how data moves and how governance can influence value creation from the local level through to cross-border exchanges. Together, these subjects can help professionals develop a more rounded understanding of what effective data governance requires. Conclusion The GIZ DataCipation data-governance courses available through atingi provide a focused learning opportunity for policymakers, regulators, public-sector professionals, IT representatives supporting policy teams and other learners interested in Africa s evolving digital and data-policy landscape. Through The African Data Economy in the Global Context , Guardians of Trust , and Unleashing Data Value: From Data Localisation to Cross-Border Data Flows , participants can explore the relationship between local data governance, continental cooperation and the global data economy. The courses address critical themes including cross-border data flows, data localisation, trusted data sharing, stakeholder participation, accountability, institutional coordination, sovereignty and the creation of economic and public value from data. Each course requires approximately 1.5 hours according to the supplied information and offers a certificate after assessment , providing a relatively accessible pathway for professionals seeking targeted learning without committing to a long-term programme. Most importantly, the training presents Africa not simply as a region responding to global digital developments, but as an active participant in defining its own approach to data governance, cooperation and value creation. There is no application or enrolment deadline stated in the information provided. Interested learners can therefore explore the courses through the atingi platform, register for an account if necessary, enrol in the relevant programme and complete the assessment requirements for certification. title: UNFPA Violence Against Women Data and Knowledge Management Specialist in Thailand – Apply for a 12-Month International UN Volunteer Assignment
summary: The United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) is seeking an experienced professional for a Violence Against Women Data and Knowledge Management Specialist assignment in Bangkok, Thailand. The opportunity is designed for a professional with strong experience in communications, knowledge management, donor reporting, research, international development programming, gender-based violence, or related areas. The assignment will support UNFPA s Asia and the Pacific Regional Office in strengthening how violence against women data and research are managed, communicated, shared, and translated into practical policy and programming action. The successful UN Volunteer will contribute to the implementation of the kNOwVAWdata initiative , a regional initiative focused on improving the ethical collection, management, analysis, dissemination, and use of violence against women data across the Asia-Pacific region. The assignment is onsite and full-time in Bangkok, Thailand , with an expected start date of 1 September 2026 and an initial duration of 12 months , with the possibility of extension. Opportunity Overview The assignment is hosted by UNFPA , the United Nations agency responsible for promoting sexual and reproductive health, advancing gender equality, supporting safe motherhood, and working toward a world where every pregnancy is wanted, every birth is safe, and every young person s potential is fulfilled. The Violence Against Women Data and Knowledge Management Specialist will work within the Asia and the Pacific Regional Gender-Based Violence and Harmful Practices team . The position focuses heavily on knowledge management, communications, digital platforms, reporting, community engagement, research dissemination, and the translation of complex violence against women data into accessible and useful information for policymakers, practitioners, researchers, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders. Assignment Details Assignment title: Violence Against Women Data and Knowledge Management Specialist Host organization: UNFPA Duty station: Bangkok, Thailand Work location: On UN premises Modality: Onsite Volunteer type: International Volunteer category: Specialist UCoS from April 2026 Work schedule: Full-time Duration: 12 months Expected start date: 1 September 2026 Possibility of extension: Yes Number of positions: 1 Recruitment: Competitive recruitment Advertisement deadline: 19 August 2026 at 03:00 Sustainable Development Goal: SDG 3 – Good Health and Well-being Language required: English About UNFPA and the Assignment Violence against women remains a major global challenge. According to the assignment description, approximately one in three women experiences physical and/or sexual violence during her lifetime, with particularly high rates reported in the Asia-Pacific region. Over the years, significant progress has been made in conducting violence against women prevalence surveys. However, important challenges remain in ensuring that data is understood, integrated across different sources, effectively communicated, and ultimately used to improve policies and programmes. To address these challenges, the UNFPA Asia and the Pacific Regional Office, in partnership with the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), is launching Phase III of the kNOwVAWdata initiative for 2026–2029 . The third phase builds on the ethical data collection foundations established during the first two phases. It places greater emphasis on creating comprehensive violence against women data ecosystems and ensuring that data and research are translated into meaningful policy and programming impact. The initiative is structured around four major pillars: Strengthening Capacity and Networks Building Integrated Data Systems Advancing Measurement Strategic Partnerships The successful volunteer will contribute to these objectives by managing knowledge platforms, supporting regional learning, strengthening professional networks, coordinating reporting, documenting impact, and making technical information more accessible. Key Responsibilities of the Violence Against Women Data and Knowledge Management Specialist The selected professional will undertake a wide range of responsibilities related to knowledge management, digital communities, communications, reporting, research, and evidence dissemination. 1. Platform Migration and Knowledge Management One of the major responsibilities will be leading the transition and migration of the kNOwVAWdata community platforms into a more modern and accessible digital environment. The volunteer will support the introduction and use of appropriate knowledge management tools to ensure that important resources can be easily accessed, organized, updated, and shared by members of the regional community. This will involve ensuring that knowledge generated through the initiative is not lost and that stakeholders can effectively find and use relevant information. 2. Microsite and Resource Maintenance The volunteer will oversee the regular maintenance and updating of the kNOwVAWdata community resources. Responsibilities will include: Updating digital resources. Restructuring information where necessary. Maintaining technical resources. Ensuring online information remains current. Supporting the accessibility and usability of knowledge resources. Helping ensure that relevant research and technical materials remain available to the intended audiences. This makes experience with web content management and digital communication particularly useful for the assignment. 3. Community of Practice Strategic Implementation The specialist will play an important role in implementing a long-term strategy for the kNOwVAWdata Community of Practice (CoP) . The objective is to develop the Community of Practice into an active, sustainable and increasingly member-led professional network. The volunteer will therefore help create an environment where members can: Exchange knowledge. Share experiences. Learn from one another. Discuss technical challenges. Develop professional connections. Exchange practical solutions. Contribute to regional knowledge. The emphasis will be on creating an organic network where participation and knowledge exchange can continue beyond individual events or projects. 4. Facilitation of Technical Working Groups Another important area of responsibility will involve moderating online forums and private interactive spaces for national survey teams. The volunteer will help facilitate member-led technical working groups focused on emerging and important issues related to violence against women data and research. Potential areas include: Technology-facilitated gender-based violence. Climate change and gender-based violence. Disability inclusion in violence against women data and research. Emerging methodological challenges. Data collection and measurement. Research and evidence utilization. The role therefore requires strong online facilitation, communication, coordination, and stakeholder engagement skills. 5. Peer-to-Peer Learning and Regional Exchange The specialist will plan, organize, and document regional learning activities. These may include: Regional webinars. South-South Cooperation initiatives. Triangular Cooperation initiatives. Peer-learning exchanges. Knowledge-sharing sessions. Technical discussions between country teams. The volunteer may interact with a wide range of stakeholders, including UNFPA Country Offices, national statistical offices, civil society organizations, researchers, and UNFPA implementing partners. The role therefore requires someone who can communicate effectively across different professional, institutional, cultural, and geographical environments. APPLY HERE. 6. Donor Reporting and Coordination A significant component of the position involves supporting donor reporting. The specialist will lead the drafting, compilation, and editorial review of high-quality narrative reports for the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) and other steering committees. The responsibilities include ensuring that reports: Clearly communicate programme progress. Present results accurately. Meet relevant donor requirements. Are professionally written and edited. Effectively communicate achievements and challenges. Follow applicable donor communication guidelines. Previous experience preparing donor reports is therefore highly relevant to this assignment. Experience working with Australian DFAT reporting requirements would be considered a strong asset. 7. Impact Documentation and Storytelling The successful candidate will also contribute to documenting the real-world impact of the kNOwVAWdata initiative. This may involve: Conducting research. Interviewing stakeholders. Writing impact stories. Producing feature articles. Developing technical briefs. Translating complex data into accessible narratives. Communicating how violence against women data contributes to changes in policy and programming. This is particularly important because the assignment requires the ability to transform complex statistical and technical information into clear and understandable content for audiences that may not have specialist technical backgrounds. Professionals with strong writing, editorial, storytelling, communications, and content development experience may therefore find this aspect of the position particularly relevant. 8. Lessons Learned and Evidence Dissemination The volunteer will support the documentation, packaging, and publication of technical and operational lessons learned from countries implementing national violence against women prevalence surveys. This may include learning from: Dedicated national prevalence surveys. Modular surveys. Administrative data system changes. Data collection initiatives. Research methodologies. Technical implementation experiences. The specialist will also contribute to regular e-bulletins that share new research, training opportunities, resources, and relevant developments with the regional community. Broader Impact of the Assignment The successful volunteer will contribute to strengthening the way violence against women data is produced, understood, communicated, and used throughout the Asia-Pacific region. The assignment aims to contribute to several important outcomes. Strengthening National Capacity The initiative seeks to strengthen national capacity for the ethical production and use of violence against women data and research. The specialist will contribute to knowledge sharing and capacity development that can help countries make better use of evidence when designing policies and programmes. Building Integrated Data Ecosystems The initiative also seeks to break down silos between different types of data. This includes improving the integration and use of: Population surveys. Administrative data. Qualitative research. Other relevant evidence sources. The ultimate goal is to create stronger and more comprehensive violence against women data ecosystems. Improving Data Literacy Another important objective is improving data literacy among: Policymakers. Advocates. Practitioners. Researchers. Other stakeholders. Improved data literacy can help bridge the gap between simply producing data and actually using that data to influence decisions and action. Advancing Inclusive Measurement The programme also seeks to advance innovative approaches to measuring violence against women. Particular attention will be given to emerging and under-researched areas, including: Technology-facilitated gender-based violence. Disability inclusion. Older women. The relationship between gender-based violence and climate change. The specialist will support knowledge management and communication around these emerging areas. Supporting Sustainable National Systems The initiative also aims to institutionalize national capacity and encourage domestic financing so that countries can maintain safe and ethical violence against women data systems over the long term. UN Volunteer Responsibilities and Volunteerism As part of the UN Volunteers programme, the selected volunteer will also be encouraged to integrate the principles of volunteerism into the assignment. This can include developing knowledge about volunteerism through UNV and external publications, participating in UNV activities, and becoming familiar with traditional and local forms of volunteerism in the host country. The volunteer may also be expected to: Provide annual and end-of-assignment self-reports. Document volunteer actions, results, and opportunities. Contribute articles and write-ups based on field experiences. Submit relevant content for UNV publications, websites, newsletters, and press releases. Assist with the UNV Buddy Programme. Promote online volunteering among relevant organizations and individuals where appropriate. Eligibility Requirements Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements before applying. Age Candidates must be between 18 and 80 years old . Nationality The candidate must be a national of a country other than Thailand , because Thailand is the country of assignment. Education Applicants must have at least a Bachelor s degree in one of the following areas: Health. Social Sciences. Gender-Based Violence. Communications. A related academic background may also be relevant where supported by the candidate s professional experience. Professional Experience The assignment requires significant professional experience. The listing indicates a minimum of 5 years of specialized experience , preferably in an international context. Relevant areas include: International development programming. Donor reporting. Strategic communications. Knowledge management. Gender equality. Gender-based violence. Research. Data and information management. Communications and advocacy. The listing also indicates a general required experience level of at least three years, while the detailed skills and experience section specifies a minimum of five years of specialized experience. Applicants should therefore use the more specific five-year requirement when assessing their suitability. CLICK HERE for more information. Language Fluency in English is required. The candidate should have excellent written and spoken English, particularly because the role involves producing reports, technical briefs, impact stories, articles, e-bulletins, and other professional communications. Preferred and Desirable Experience Although not every item listed below is mandatory, candidates with these experiences may have a stronger profile. UN system experience Prior experience working within the UN system is highly desirable, particularly experience related to: Gender equality. Gender-based violence. Demographic statistics. International development. The Asia-Pacific region. Online Community Management Experience establishing, moderating, and sustaining: Online communities of practice. Professional networks. Knowledge portals. Interactive online forums. would be particularly valuable. Editorial and Writing Skills The role requires strong editorial judgment and the ability to turn complex technical information into clear and accessible content. Applicants should be comfortable producing: Narrative reports. Technical briefs. Feature articles. Impact stories. E-bulletins. Knowledge products. Digital content. Donor Reporting Applicants with experience preparing high-quality donor reports are encouraged to apply. Knowledge of Australian DFAT reporting guidelines is specifically identified as a strong asset. Digital and Computer Skills Strong computer literacy is required. Experience with tools and platforms such as: Google Workspace. Microsoft Office. Email and internet platforms. Data and information management systems. Web content management systems. is relevant to the assignment. Design Skills Knowledge of basic design and digital production tools is desirable. Examples mentioned in the assignment include: Canva. Adobe Creative Suite. InDesign. This could be useful when preparing report layouts, knowledge products, digital assets, and other communication materials. Core Competencies The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate a range of professional and interpersonal competencies. Professionalism The candidate should demonstrate sound professional judgment, technical knowledge, discretion, diplomacy, and the ability to work independently. The role requires someone who can take initiative, manage information objectively and confidentially, coordinate with multiple stakeholders, and take ownership of responsibilities. Integrity Applicants should demonstrate commitment to UN values and ethical standards. This includes acting professionally, resisting inappropriate pressure, exercising sound judgment, and responding appropriately to unethical or unprofessional conduct. Teamwork and Respect for Diversity The specialist will work with people from different cultures, professional backgrounds, nationalities, genders, and institutions. Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to develop respectful working relationships are therefore essential. The candidate should demonstrate sensitivity to cultural and individual differences and a commitment to gender equality and inclusion. Planning and Organization The assignment involves managing multiple activities and potentially competing deadlines. The successful candidate should be able to: Prioritize tasks. Organize activities. Manage multiple projects. Coordinate stakeholders. Monitor progress. Meet deadlines. Work effectively under pressure. Communication Excellent communication skills are central to the role. The specialist should be able to communicate clearly with different audiences and prepare concise, high-quality written materials. Presentation skills, stakeholder communication, knowledge transfer, and the ability to explain complex information to non-technical audiences are also important. Commitment to Volunteerism The candidate should have a genuine commitment to the principles of volunteer engagement, including solidarity, compassion, reciprocity, and self-reliance. A commitment to the mission and values of UNFPA and the wider UN system is also expected. Working Environment and Duty Station The assignment will be based in Bangkok, Thailand and will be performed onsite on UN premises. According to the assignment information, Bangkok is a highly developed modern city with a wide range of accommodation options, including apartments and houses. The cost of living is described as relatively high compared with some other Asian capitals, although it remains lower than many cities in Europe and North America. The city has well-developed health facilities and services and strong international connectivity, with regular flights linking Bangkok to major cities around the world. title: Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship 2026–2027: 50% Tuition Fee Scholarship for International Students in Australia.
summary: International students looking for an opportunity to study in Australia can apply for the Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship , a competitive scholarship offering a substantial reduction in tuition fees for outstanding students beginning eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programmes. The scholarship is offered by Griffith University in Queensland, Australia , and is designed to recognize and support exceptional international students commencing their studies at the university. Successful recipients receive a scholarship covering 50% of their tuition fees for the duration of their eligible degree, subject to meeting the university s ongoing scholarship and enrolment requirements. The scholarship is available for students commencing eligible programmes in 2026 or 2027 and can provide significant financial support throughout the student s degree. For students commencing in Trimester 3, 2026 , the application deadline is 15 August 2026 . Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship 2026–2027 The Vice Chancellor s International Scholarship is designed for high-achieving international students who are preparing to begin undergraduate or postgraduate coursework studies at Griffith University. The scholarship recognizes students who have demonstrated strong academic performance and provides financial assistance toward their tuition fees. Rather than being a one-time payment, the scholarship can remain valid throughout the student s degree, provided the recipient continues to satisfy the required conditions. Scholarship Overview Scholarship name: Vice Chancellor s International Scholarship University: Griffith University Country: Australia Study level: Undergraduate and postgraduate coursework Scholarship value: 50% of tuition fees Duration: Whole degree, subject to ongoing eligibility Study mode: Full-time Available intakes: 2026 and 2027 Eligible students: International students Nationality restriction: Citizens of Australia and New Zealand are not eligible Scholarship type: Competitive Study location: Griffith University campuses in Queensland Deadline: Depends on the commencing trimester What Does the Griffith University Scholarship Cover? The Vice Chancellor s International Scholarship provides a 50% reduction in tuition fees . The scholarship applies to eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees for the duration of the student s programme, subject to the recipient continuing to meet the scholarship requirements. This means students do not receive a cash payment for general living expenses. Instead, the scholarship reduces the amount of eligible tuition fees they are required to pay. Students remain responsible for the remaining tuition fees and other costs associated with studying in Australia. How Long Does the Scholarship Last? The scholarship is valid for the student s whole degree , provided the student continues to meet the ongoing eligibility and enrolment requirements. The applicable course duration is based on the programme length stated in the student s Letter of Offer, taking into account any credit received for previous study. Scholarship deductions are applied by the census date of the relevant trimester. Who Can Apply for the Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship? The scholarship is specifically designed for international students. Applicants must satisfy several conditions before they can be considered. International Student Requirement Applicants must be citizens of a country other than Australia or New Zealand . This means the opportunity is open to eligible students from many parts of the world, including countries in: Africa Asia Europe North America South America The Middle East Oceania Other regions outside Australia and New Zealand The scholarship does not identify a particular race or ethnic group as a requirement. The key nationality requirement is that the applicant must not be an Australian or New Zealand citizen. Academic Requirement Applicants must have achieved a minimum GPA of 6.0 on a 7-point scale , or an equivalent academic result under their previous education system. This is an important requirement because the scholarship is competitive and is intended to support outstanding international students. Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic records clearly demonstrate their eligibility. Admission Requirement Students must first apply to study an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme at Griffith University. To apply for the scholarship, the student must have received an offer to study by the applicable scholarship application closing date. The process therefore involves two related applications: Apply for admission to Griffith University. Once an offer has been received, submit the scholarship application before the relevant deadline. Students should not wait until the scholarship deadline to begin the university admission process. English Language Requirement Applicants must satisfy Griffith University s academic and English language entry requirements for their selected programme. The exact English-language requirements can vary depending on the degree. Students should therefore check the entry requirements for their specific undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme before applying. Full-Time Study Requirement The scholarship is intended for students beginning their studies on a full-time basis . Recipients must continue to meet the university s enrolment and academic progression requirements in order to retain the scholarship. Which Study Levels Are Eligible? The scholarship is available for eligible: Undergraduate coursework programmes. Postgraduate coursework programmes. This makes the opportunity relevant to both students seeking their first university degree and students looking to pursue further coursework-based studies. However, not every Griffith University programme qualifies. Programmes Excluded from the Scholarship The scholarship terms and conditions specifically exclude several categories of study. The scholarship does not apply to: Higher Degree Research programmes. Online programmes where the campus is listed as online. Non-award programmes. Study Abroad Programmes. Diploma programmes. Masters Qualifying Programmes. MBA programme code 5158. English language programmes at Griffith English Language Institute. Programmes offered only on a part-time basis. Programmes delivered onshore or offshore in collaboration with a partner organization. Applicants should therefore check that their specific programme is eligible before applying. Griffith University Scholarship Deadlines The application deadline depends on the trimester in which the student plans to begin studying. Trimester 2, 2026 Application deadline: 11 April 2026 Scholarship outcome: 29 April 2026 Trimester starts: 13 July 2026 This deadline has already passed. Trimester 3, 2026 For students planning to begin their studies in Trimester 3, 2026: Application deadline: 15 August 2026 Scholarship outcome: 28 August 2026 Trimester starts: 2 November 2026 This is the upcoming deadline for 2026 applicants based on the information provided. Trimester 1, 2027 Students commencing in Trimester 1, 2027 have the following timeline: Application deadline: 28 November 2026 Scholarship outcome: 11 December 2026 Trimester starts: 1 March 2027 Australian Year 12 Students Students completing Australian Year 12 have a separate deadline: Application deadline: 21 December 2026 Scholarship outcome: 24 December 2026 Trimester starts: 1 March 2027 The Australian Year 12 deadline is specifically identified for students in that category. How to Apply for the Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship The application process involves several stages. Step 1: Choose an Eligible Griffith University Programme First, prospective students should identify an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme at Griffith University. Applicants should check: Academic entry requirements. English language requirements. Programme duration. Campus location. Study mode. Intake dates. Scholarship eligibility. Step 2: Apply for Admission The applicant must submit an application to study at Griffith University. The university provides an international student application process through its official website. Step 3: Receive a Letter of Offer Applicants need to receive their Letter of Offer before applying for the scholarship by the relevant closing date. This is an important part of the process because the scholarship is intended for new students who are commencing an eligible programme. Step 4: Apply for the Scholarship Once the student has received their offer, they can apply for the Vice Chancellor s International Scholarship. The scholarship application requires academic records and a personal statement . Step 5: Scholarship Assessment Eligible applications are reviewed by a university panel. Because the scholarship is competitive and the number of scholarships is limited, meeting the minimum requirements does not automatically guarantee selection. What Should the Personal Statement Include? Applicants are required to provide a personal statement as part of the scholarship application. A strong personal statement should clearly communicate the student s academic background, achievements, aspirations, and reasons for pursuing their chosen programme. Applicants should aim to demonstrate: Academic excellence. Motivation for their chosen field. Clear educational goals. Career aspirations. Why Griffith University is a suitable institution. How the programme fits their future plans. What makes them a strong scholarship candidate. The statement should be clear, specific, and supported by genuine examples from the applicant s academic or professional background. How Competitive Is the Scholarship? The Vice Chancellor s International Scholarship is a competitive scholarship . Griffith University has a limited number of scholarships available. This means that even students who meet the minimum GPA and eligibility requirements are not automatically guaranteed an award. The university states that once the available scholarship acceptances have been reached, applicants may be informed that all available scholarships have been awarded and the scholarships withdrawn. Students should therefore apply as early as possible and ensure that their application is complete and competitive. CLICK HERE for more information. What Happens After You Receive the Scholarship? Successful applicants must accept both: Their Griffith University programme offer. Their scholarship offer. Both must be accepted by the deadlines specified in the student s Scholarship Letter. If the student fails to accept the scholarship within the specified timeframe, the scholarship can be withdrawn. How Is the Scholarship Applied? Once the student begins studying at Griffith University, the scholarship is applied toward eligible tuition fees before the census date of each trimester, provided the student continues to meet the requirements. The student is responsible for paying the remaining tuition fee balance by the applicable census date. The scholarship therefore significantly reduces tuition costs but does not necessarily cover the entire cost of studying in Australia. Ongoing Requirements to Keep the Scholarship Receiving the scholarship is only the beginning. Students must continue meeting specific academic and enrolment requirements throughout their degree. Maintain Full-Time Enrolment Students must remain enrolled full-time unless credit from previous study prevents full-time enrolment. They must also comply with the requirements of their programme and student visa. Make Satisfactory Academic Progress Recipients must successfully progress through their programme. They are expected to pass all courses for each trimester and continue into the next trimester. Maintain the Required GPA Students must maintain a minimum cumulative GPA of 5.5 on a 7.0 scale annually to qualify for scholarship tuition deductions in the following year. The cumulative GPA is calculated using grades awarded across the student s programme, with only courses graded with a GPA included in the calculation. Remain in the Approved Programme Students must remain enrolled in the programme for which the scholarship was awarded. The approved programme is identified in the Letter of Offer issued by Griffith International Admissions. Changing to a different programme may affect scholarship eligibility. What Happens If a Student Withdraws? If a scholarship recipient withdraws or cancels their studies for any reason, the scholarship amount is non-refundable . Students should therefore carefully consider their programme and study plans before accepting the scholarship. Deferral of the Scholarship Deferral of the scholarship is not permitted. Students should therefore ensure that they are ready to commence their programme in the trimester for which the scholarship has been awarded. The scholarship is linked to the relevant commencement period. International Fee-Paying Student Requirement Students must maintain International Fee Paying status to qualify for the scholarship and each scholarship deduction. If the student s fee-paying status changes, the scholarship may no longer be available. This is particularly important for international students because the scholarship is specifically designed to provide financial assistance to eligible international fee-paying students. Other Important Scholarship Conditions Recipients should be aware of additional terms and conditions. The scholarship: Applies only to eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees. Does not cover general living expenses. Does not cover excluded programmes. Cannot be deferred. Is competitive. Has a limited number of awards available. Requires students to meet ongoing academic and enrolment requirements. Requires recipients to comply with their student visa requirements. Recipients may also be profiled in Griffith University marketing activities . Why Apply for the Griffith University Scholarship? The Vice Chancellor s International Scholarship can provide significant financial assistance to international students who are planning to study in Australia. 50% Tuition Fee Reduction The most significant benefit is the 50% tuition fee scholarship . For students facing international tuition fees, reducing the tuition component by half can substantially lower the financial burden of completing a degree. Support Throughout the Degree The scholarship can remain valid for the entire eligible programme rather than being limited to the first year, provided the recipient meets the continuing requirements. Study at Griffith University Recipients have the opportunity to study at Griffith University in Queensland, Australia. The university has campuses including Brisbane City, Brisbane South (Nathan), Gold Coast and Logan. The exact campus depends on the student s selected programme. Undergraduate and Postgraduate Options Unlike scholarships limited to a particular academic level, this scholarship is available for both undergraduate and postgraduate coursework programmes, subject to the exclusions. International Academic Experience International students can gain academic experience in Australia while developing their knowledge, skills, professional networks, and international exposure. Important Financial Considerations Although the scholarship covers 50% of eligible tuition fees, applicants should understand that it is not a fully funded scholarship . Students will generally need to cover the remaining tuition fees as well as other expenses associated with studying and living in Australia. Potential costs may include: Remaining tuition fees. Accommodation. Food. Transportation. Health-related costs. Student visa-related expenses. Study materials. Personal expenses. Other living costs. Applicants should therefore prepare a realistic financial plan before accepting the scholarship. APPLY HERE. Who Should Apply? The scholarship may be particularly suitable for international students who: Have strong academic results. Are planning to study an eligible undergraduate coursework programme. Are planning to study an eligible postgraduate coursework programme. Want to study in Australia. Can meet Griffith University s English language requirements. Have received or can obtain a Griffith University offer before the scholarship deadline. Can meet the financial requirements for the portion of tuition and living expenses not covered by the scholarship. Are prepared to study full-time. Can maintain the required academic performance throughout their degree. Tips for Preparing a Strong Application Applicants should avoid treating the scholarship application as simply a formality. Because the scholarship is competitive, students should make their application as strong and complete as possible. 1. Apply for Admission Early Do not wait until the scholarship deadline to begin the university application. Remember that applicants need an offer to study by the scholarship closing date. 2. Choose an Eligible Programme Make sure your selected programme is not among the excluded courses. 4. Prepare a Strong Personal Statement Use the personal statement to demonstrate your academic achievements, motivation, future goals, and reasons for choosing Griffith University. 5. Check English Requirements Make sure you meet the English-language requirements of your chosen programme. 6. Apply Before the Deadline Do not wait until the final hours to submit your application.
