title: JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship Program 2026 in Japan and Thailand: Fully Funded Research Opportunity for Developing Countries
summary: Applications are now open for the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship Program FY2026 , an international research fellowship offering qualified researchers from developing countries the opportunity to undertake advanced scientific research in Japan or Thailand . Organized by the Japan International Research Center for Agricultural Sciences (JIRCAS) , the fellowship is designed to accelerate scientific research while strengthening the expertise and research capabilities of selected researchers from developing countries. Successful fellows will work on designated research themes under the supervision and guidance of JIRCAS researchers. For the FY2026 intake, JIRCAS is accepting applications for five research themes covering areas including maize and biological nitrification inhibition, methane fermentation and microbial systems, mungbean genetics, phosphate-solubilizing microorganisms, and sugarcane responses to climate-related stresses. Depending on the selected research theme, successful fellows will undertake their research either at JIRCAS in Tsukuba, Japan, or at a JIRCAS project site in Thailand . The fellowship will run for one year beginning in November 2026 and provides significant financial and logistical support, including a round-trip economy-class airline ticket, a daily living allowance of JPY 7,700 , housing support and overseas travel accident insurance. Interested researchers should pay particular attention to the application timeline. Both registration and submission of the required application documents must be completed by the official deadline. Application Deadline: August 31, 2026, at 5:00 PM Japan Standard Time (JST). About the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship Program The JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship Program is one of the initiatives implemented by the Japan International Research Center for Agricultural Sciences to promote scientific research and strengthen the expertise of nominated researchers from developing countries. Rather than functioning solely as a financial award, the program provides selected researchers with an opportunity to actively conduct research under the supervision of JIRCAS scientists. This structure gives fellows the chance to participate directly in specialized research while developing their expertise through collaboration with researchers working in relevant scientific fields. For FY2026, applicants must select from the research themes officially identified by JIRCAS. Each theme has its own research focus, host scientist and location. JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship 2026 Research Themes There are five research themes available for the FY2026 fellowship program . Theme 1: BNI-Release Mechanisms in Maize The first research theme is titled: BNI-Release Mechanisms in Maize – Analyzing the Role of Plasma Membrane H+-ATPase Activity in Genetic Differences for BNI-Capacity in Maize. Research toward developing BNI-enabled maize has involved maize lines demonstrating contrasting Biological Nitrification Inhibition capacities, particularly the high-BNI line CML-133 and low-BNI line CML-484 . A total of 164 doubled haploid lines have been developed from these parental lines. The research examines differences in rhizosphere nitrogen dynamics and growth responses between the parental lines. The release of BNI compounds is enhanced primarily under NH4+ conditions, and the research investigates the hypothesis that activation of plasma membrane H+-ATPase plays an important role in the release mechanism. The project seeks to clarify the functional relationship between H+-ATPase activity and the release of BNI compounds. The resulting research is expected to contribute fundamental knowledge toward developing BNI-enabled maize. The selected JIRCAS fellow will be expected to participate actively in ongoing BNI research and contribute to evaluation of the doubled haploid population being investigated by the host researcher. Host Scientist: Guntur Venkata Subbarao Research Location: Tsukuba, Japan Theme 2: Development of Methanogenic Microbial Consortia and Stable Cultivation Technology The second research theme focuses on the: Development of Methanogenic Microbial Consortia Adapted to Microbial Saccharification Conditions and Stable Cultivation Technology. This research aims to develop an integrated saccharification-methane fermentation biomethane platform by combining microbial saccharification with methane fermentation. Researchers are screening methanogens capable of functioning under conditions suitable for saccharifying microorganisms. The evaluation seeks to identify new methanogenic microbial communities and determine methanogenic systems that demonstrate greater compatibility with the saccharification process. The project also investigates technologies relating to the immobilization and stable cultivation of methanogens. The broader objective is to establish an efficient technological foundation connecting the decomposition of solid biomass with methane production. The selected fellow will be involved in activities including: Screening methanogenic strains; Characterizing methanogenic strains and microbial communities derived from environmental samples; Assessing their suitability under saccharification conditions; Evaluating interactions with saccharifying microorganisms; Measuring methane-production performance; Investigating immobilization characteristics; Investigating granule formation; and Assessing the stability of methane production during cultivation. Host Scientist: UKE Ayaka Research Location: Tsukuba, Japan Theme 3: Screening and Mechanistic Evaluation of Mungbean Emergence Under Soil Crust Conditions Theme 3 focuses on identifying mungbean (Vigna radiata) genetic resources capable of demonstrating superior emergence under soil crust conditions and understanding the physiological and genetic mechanisms responsible for this ability. Soil crusting can create a major challenge for establishing legume crops in semi-arid tropical environments. Heavy rainfall followed by rapid drying can produce a hard surface layer that physically restricts seedlings from emerging successfully. Under this research program, a core collection consisting of 96 mungbean accessions will be screened under controlled crust conditions. Researchers will evaluate factors including: Emergence rate; Hypocotyl thrust; Seedling vigour; and Related seed characteristics, including phytic acid content. Accessions displaying contrasting responses will subsequently undergo more detailed examination to determine which traits govern their ability to penetrate crusted soil. The findings will also be compared with parallel soybean data to investigate whether these mechanisms are conserved across different legume species. Ultimately, the research is expected to produce validated screening protocols and identify promising germplasm that could contribute to breeding varieties better adapted to soils susceptible to crusting. Host Scientist: NAKAGAWA Andressa Research Location: Tsukuba, Japan Theme 4: Isolation of Elite Phosphate-Solubilizing Rhizosphere Microorganisms The fourth research theme is: Isolation of Elite Phosphate-Solubilizing Rhizosphere Microorganisms and Elucidation of Their Synergistic Interactions with Rhizobia in Tropical Cropping Systems. This research focuses on isolating and selecting elite phosphate-solubilizing microorganisms from the rhizosphere of tropical legume and cereal crops. Researchers will evaluate the microorganisms ability to promote plant growth when used together with rhizobia. Major areas of investigation include: Phosphate-solubilizing activity; Effects of co-inoculation with rhizobia; Molecular mechanisms associated with microbial performance; Physiological mechanisms underlying microbial performance; and Plant-microbe interactions. The expected results should contribute fundamental scientific knowledge that could help improve the functionality of microbial materials used for sustainable soil fertility management. The research is closely connected to the B6 project concerning African rice-based agriculture, which aims to develop sustainable technologies using beneficial microbial resources. JIRCAS provides facilities necessary for activities including nutrient analysis, molecular biological experiments, greenhouse trials and growth chamber experiments. Host Scientist: Papa Saliou Sarr Research Location: Tsukuba, Japan Theme 5: Physiological and Genetic Responses of Sugarcane Under Multi-Stress Conditions Theme 5 focuses on the: Evaluation of Physiological and Genetic Responses of Sugarcane under Multi-stress Conditions. Climate change is intensifying multiple abiotic stresses affecting sugarcane production across Southeast Asia, particularly salinity, drought and flooding . This research will examine the growth, physiological and genetic responses of sugarcane exposed to combined stress conditions. The objective is to develop robust evaluation indices that could help strengthen multi-stress tolerance within sugarcane breeding programs. Working alongside researchers from JIRCAS and the Khon Kaen Field Crops Research Center (KKFCRC) , the selected fellow will undertake comparative assessments examining sugarcane responses under both individual and combined stress conditions. Beyond generating scientific knowledge, the initiative also aims to develop researchers capable of contributing to and potentially leading regional sugarcane research networks throughout Southeast Asia. Host Scientist: TAKARAGAWA Hiroo Research Location: Thailand Applicants interested in Theme 5 should carefully note that the researcher will be based in Thailand. JIRCAS states that Thai nationals or applicants eligible to stay in Thailand for one year will be given preference for this particular theme. List of Research Themes JIRCAS Fellowship Program FY2026.pdf Eligibility Requirements for the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship 2026 Applicants must satisfy several requirements established by JIRCAS. 1. Citizenship Requirement Applicants must be citizens of a developing country . 2. Current Employment and Research Requirement Applicants must currently be employed by a research organization or university in their home country and must be actively involved in research related to: Agriculture; Forestry; or Fisheries. After completing the fellowship, the researcher must be willing to return to their home country and continue their research at the same research institute or university. 3. Academic Qualification Applicants should possess at least a Master s degree (MSc) in a relevant field connected to: Socio-economics; Natural sciences; or Technology. 4. Research Commitment Applicants must be able to work exclusively on the research theme for which they apply during the fellowship. 5. Health Requirement Applicants should be in good health. 6. Language Requirements Applicants are required to possess an adequate command of English and/or Japanese . 7. Institutional Endorsement Candidates must receive endorsement from the appropriate authority at the institution where they are employed or affiliated. 8. Special Condition for Theme 5 Theme 5 will be conducted in Thailand. Consequently, applicants who are Thai nationals or otherwise eligible to remain in Thailand for one year will receive preference for this research theme. Duration of the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship 2026 The JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship has a duration of one year . The FY2026 fellowship is scheduled to begin in November 2026 . Applicants should therefore consider their professional responsibilities, institutional commitments and ability to dedicate themselves exclusively to the selected research theme before applying. Financial Benefits of the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship 2026 The fellowship provides several important benefits to successful researchers. 1. Round-Trip Airfare JIRCAS will provide a round-trip economy-class airline ticket . However, airfare is not provided for dependents accompanying the fellow. 2. Daily Living Allowance Successful fellows will receive a living allowance of: JPY 7,700 per day The stated daily living allowance excludes the housing allowance. 3. Housing Support A housing allowance will be provided according to government housing regulations. Living facilities will also be provided. For fellows undertaking their research in Tsukuba, Japan , the listed accommodation facility is: Tsukuba International House (TIH) 2-1-9 Kannondai Tsukuba, Ibaraki 305-0856 Japan For fellows based in Thailand , the source states that the accommodation facility is yet to be determined. 4. Insurance Coverage The fellowship provides an overseas travel accident insurance package covering injury, sickness and damage. Applicants should note, however, that the insurance does not cover: Chronic diseases; Dental treatment; Pregnancy; or Childbirth. How to Apply for the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship 2026 JIRCAS has established a three-step application procedure . Applicants should carefully complete every stage because both registration and submission must be completed by the application deadline. Step 1: Complete the Online Registration Form Applicants must first register their application by completing the JIRCAS Online Registration Form for the FY2026 Visiting Research Fellowship Program. Step 2: Wait for Registration Confirmation and Submission Instructions Following registration, applicants will receive an email from JIRCAS confirming their registration. This email will also provide guidance concerning the submission of application documents. Step 3: Submit All Required Documents Applicants must then submit the required documents to JIRCAS by email , following the instructions provided after registration. APPLY NOW Required Documents for the JIRCAS Fellowship Application Applicants are required to prepare and submit the following seven items: 1. Summary of Ongoing Research Applicants must provide a summary of the research they are currently undertaking at their institute or university . JIRCAS provides an official application template for this requirement. 2. Summary of Proposed Research Applicants must submit a summary describing the research they propose to undertake through the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship Program . An official template is also available for this document. 3. List of Publications Applicants must provide a list of their publications using the relevant JIRCAS application documentation. 4. Institutional Endorsement Letter An endorsement letter signed by the appropriate authority at the applicant s institute or university must be submitted. This requirement corresponds with the program s eligibility condition requiring institutional endorsement. 5. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must provide a CV of no more than two pages . JIRCAS allows the CV to be prepared in any format but specifically states that certificates should not be attached to the CV. 6. Recent Photograph A recent photograph of the applicant must be submitted. 7. Three Relevant Publications Applicants must submit copies of the three publications most relevant to their application and proposed research . Applicants should prepare these documents carefully and ensure that the information in their proposed research summary demonstrates clear relevance to the research theme they have selected. JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship 2026 Application Deadline The official deadline for the FY2026 JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship is: August 31, 2026, at 5:00 PM Japan Standard Time (JST). Importantly, JIRCAS states that both registration and submission must be completed by this deadline . Applicants should therefore avoid treating registration alone as completion of the application process. When Will JIRCAS Announce the Fellowship Results? Applicants are expected to receive notification regarding the outcome of their applications by September 24, 2026 . The results will be communicated to applicants by email. Successful candidates should subsequently prepare for the fellowship, which is scheduled to begin in November 2026. Important Points Applicants Should Remember Before submitting an application for the JIRCAS Visiting Research Fellowship Program FY2026, prospective candidates should carefully consider the following: The fellowship targets researchers from developing countries. Applicants must currently work at a research organization or university in their home country. Their active research must relate to agriculture, forestry or fisheries. Applicants should possess at least an MSc in an appropriate field. Candidates must select and commit to one of the specified FY2026 research themes. The fellowship lasts for one year beginning in November 2026. Most research themes are based in Tsukuba, Japan, while Theme 5 is based in Thailand. Institutional endorsement is required. Applicants must possess adequate English and/or Japanese language ability. The application requires seven supporting items, including research summaries, publications, a CV, photograph and institutional endorsement. Both registration and document submission must be completed by August 31, 2026, at 5:00 PM JST . Results are expected to be communicated by email by September 24, 2026 . JIRCAS Fellowship 2026 Inquiries Applicants who have questions about the fellowship should use the inquiry form available on the JIRCAS website and identify their inquiry as relating to the “Visiting Research Fellow.” Prospective applicants should note that JIRCAS specifically states that inquiries relating to the research themes will not be answered . title: Kohli Fellowship for Sociology 2026–2028: Fully Funded Two-Year Postdoctoral Research Opportunity in Berlin or Florence.
summary: The Kohli Foundation for Sociology is offering the Kohli Fellowship for Sociology , a prestigious postdoctoral research opportunity designed to support outstanding early-career sociologists following the completion of their PhD. The fellowship provides financial support for a two-year postdoctoral stay at either the WZB in Berlin, Germany , or the European University Institute (EUI) in Fiesole/Florence, Italy . The opportunity is designed to give recently graduated sociology scholars the time, institutional environment, academic networks, and resources needed to develop a new research project, strengthen their publication record, establish research collaborations, and advance their academic careers. Scholars from all nationalities are eligible to apply, provided their research relates to the research programme of the respective host institution and they meet the fellowship s doctoral-degree requirements. The Kohli Foundation particularly encourages applications from women and scholars belonging to academically underrepresented groups . One fellow is selected each year. Overview of the Kohli Fellowship for Sociology The Kohli Fellowship is part of the Kohli Foundation s broader Growth programme, which focuses on supporting early-career researchers in sociology. The Growth programme is intended for sociologists who are either pursuing a PhD or have completed their PhD within the previous five years. Through its fellowship and funding activities, the foundation aims to help early-career sociologists strengthen their academic development, expand professional networks, advance their research, and build stronger academic profiles. The Kohli Fellowship specifically supports researchers who have successfully completed their doctoral dissertation with excellent results and are ready to take the next step in their academic careers. What Does the Kohli Fellowship Provide? The fellowship supports a two-year postdoctoral research stay at one of two prestigious European research institutions: WZB Berlin Social Science Center (WZB), Berlin European University Institute (EUI), Fiesole/Florence During the fellowship, researchers are expected to develop a new research project while advancing their academic publications and building research collaborations. The fellowship therefore goes beyond simply providing financial support. It is structured to place researchers within an active academic environment where they can interact with established scholars, participate in intellectual activities, attend conferences and training programmes, and develop their academic networks. Kohli Fellowship at the European University Institute Researchers selected for the EUI placement will become part of the Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies . As a Kohli Fellow at the EUI, the researcher will be appointed to one of the EUI faculties and will have an academic advisor who will support the fellow in developing and expanding their qualifications. The fellowship provides opportunities to work on an independent research project while participating in the broader academic life of the institute. Activities and Opportunities at the EUI As part of their fellowship, researchers may have opportunities to: Conduct fieldwork related to their research project. Participate in internal training. Attend national and international conferences. Organize their own academic workshop. Connect with other postdoctoral researchers. Participate in Max Weber Programme events. Develop academic and professional collaborations. Strengthen their research and publication profile. The EUI environment is therefore designed to provide both research independence and access to a broader community of postdoctoral scholars and established academics. EUI Fellowship Timeline The information provided outlines the following timeline for the EUI pathway: Fall 2027: Deadline for the application for the Max Weber Programme. Winter 2027/2028: Interviews, selection, and notification of fellows. 1 September 2028: Fellowship starts at the EUI. Applicants interested in the EUI route should therefore pay close attention to the relevant Max Weber Programme application timeline. Kohli Fellowship at the WZB in Berlin The second host institution is the WZB in Berlin . A Kohli Fellow at the WZB will become part of a vibrant intellectual research community and participate in the scholarly activities of their host research unit. Each fellow will have a contact person among WZB staff who can provide support throughout the fellowship. The WZB pathway is designed to give the researcher an environment in which they can focus on their research while also developing their academic career. Activities and Opportunities at the WZB Within the fellowship, researchers may have opportunities to: Conduct fieldwork. Participate in internal training seminars. Attend national conferences. Attend international conferences. Organize an academic workshop. Engage with researchers within their host research unit. Develop research collaborations. Receive support for their individual career-development needs. Participate actively in the intellectual life of the institution. WZB Fellowship Timeline The information provided gives the following timeline for the WZB fellowship: Fall 2026: Deadline for applications for the Kohli Fellowship for Sociology at WZB. Winter 2026/2027: Interviews, selection, and notification of fellows. 1 October 2027: Fellowship begins at WZB. Applicants interested in the WZB option should therefore prepare their application ahead of the Fall 2026 deadline and monitor the official application process for the exact closing date. Who Can Apply for the Kohli Fellowship? The fellowship is open to scholars of all nationalities . However, applicants must satisfy several academic and research requirements. Nationality The foundation explicitly states that scholars of all nationalities are eligible to apply. This means the opportunity is not restricted to applicants from Europe, North America, Africa, Asia, Latin America, or any other particular region. Researchers from any country or continent can be considered if they meet the academic and research requirements. APPLY HERE. Doctoral Degree Requirement Applicants must have held their doctoral degree for no longer than five years before the starting date of the fellowship . This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to researchers who have recently completed their PhD and are transitioning into the postdoctoral stage of their careers. Applicants must also have: Submitted their doctoral dissertation. Successfully defended their dissertation. Completed these requirements before the fellowship contract begins. Research Area Applicants should have research that relates to the research programme of the respective host institution. The foundation particularly welcomes research projects focusing on: Life-course issues. Generational issues. However, applicants are not limited to these topics. The foundation states that other research topics are equally considered , provided the research is relevant to the academic programme of the host institution. What Documents Are Required? Applicants for the Kohli Fellowship should prepare several important documents. The application should include: 1. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must submit a CV that includes their academic and professional background. The CV should also include a list of publications . Applicants should ensure that their publication record is presented clearly, particularly where they have peer-reviewed articles, books, book chapters, working papers, or other significant academic outputs. 2. Academic Career Statement Applicants must provide an Academic Career Statement . This should help the selection committee understand the applicant s academic trajectory, achievements, development, and future career direction. 3. Research Proposal The research proposal is a central component of the application. It should outline the research project the applicant intends to pursue as a Kohli Fellow. A strong proposal should clearly demonstrate: The research question. The significance of the research. The proposed approach. The contribution to sociology. The relevance to the host institution. How the fellowship period will advance the project. Potential academic outputs and collaborations. 4. Academic Referees Applicants must provide the names of two to three academic referees . Applicants should contact their referees in advance and obtain their agreement to provide a reference letter if requested. It is therefore important not to list academic referees without first confirming their availability and willingness to support the application. How Are Kohli Fellows Selected? Successful candidates are selected in close consultation with the relevant academic host institution. The selection process considers several factors. Scholarly Excellence Academic excellence is an important consideration. The foundation seeks researchers who have demonstrated strong academic performance and successfully completed their doctoral research. Quality of the Research Proposal The proposed research project is another major component of the selection process. The proposal should outline a strong project that can realistically be pursued during the fellowship period and contribute meaningfully to the applicant s academic development. Interview Candidates are also expected to participate in an interview. The interview may take place: In person, or By video. The selection process therefore assesses both the written application and the candidate s ability to discuss their research and academic plans. Expectations During the Fellowship Kohli Fellows are expected to actively participate in the intellectual life of their host institution. This means the fellowship is not intended simply as an independent period of research away from academic communities. Fellows are expected to engage with colleagues, participate in academic activities, and make use of the research environment provided by their host institution. Fellows are also expected to reside in either Berlin or Florence , depending on their placement. For more information on Kohli Fellowship for Sociology 2026–2028 VISIT HERE. Current and Previous Kohli Fellows The Kohli Foundation has already supported several researchers through the fellowship. Flavien Ganter – Kohli Fellow at EUI, 2025–2027 Flavien Ganter received the third Kohli Fellowship for Sociology. He completed his PhD in Sociology at Columbia University in 2025 and also graduated from the École normale supérieure at Paris-Saclay and the École nationale de la statistique et de l’administration économique. His research uses original experiments and census data to examine how social cleavages that cross ethnoracial categories can reshape ethnoracial boundaries in the United States. Alexander Hoppe – Kohli Fellow at WZB, 2024–2026 Alexander Hoppe received the second Kohli Fellowship. He completed his PhD at the University of Pennsylvania and subsequently worked as a postdoctoral researcher at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Societies . His research focuses on the microfoundations of capitalism, with particular interest in the fashion industry. His book project, Making Mass Fashion , examines the origins of fashion and the role of anticipation in shaping the labour process. Camille Portier – Kohli Fellow at EUI, 2023–2025 Camille Portier was the first Kohli Fellow for Sociology. She completed her PhD at Cornell University in 2023 and previously earned an MSc in Sociology from the University of Oxford . At the EUI, her research shifted from examining how occupational characteristics influence people s outcomes and life chances toward studying work contexts and occupational outcomes that structure careers across the life course. Support for Women and Underrepresented Scholars The Kohli Foundation particularly welcomes applications from women and scholars belonging to academically underrepresented groups . This reflects the foundation s interest in supporting broader participation and representation within academic sociology. However, applicants should still demonstrate the required academic excellence, relevant research fit, and qualifications outlined in the fellowship requirements. Connect Funding Program for Early-Career Sociologists In addition to the Kohli Fellowship, the Kohli Foundation for Sociology operates the Connect funding programme . Connect is designed to support events and structured exchange programmes that promote the academic development and professional growth of early-career sociologists. The programme recognizes that career development in academia involves more than individual research. Professional networks, mentoring relationships, academic events, workshops, and opportunities to exchange ideas with established scholars can play an important role in helping early-career researchers develop their careers. What Does Connect Funding Support? The Connect programme supports events that: Promote academic development. Support professional growth. Facilitate the advancement of independent research projects. Maintain a high academic standard. Connect early-career researchers with established research networks. Connect researchers with academic institutions. Strengthen networking among early-career researchers. Create opportunities to interact with established and renowned sociologists. The programme specifically focuses on activities that provide meaningful academic and professional benefits to researchers at an early stage of their careers. Types of Events Eligible for Connect Funding The Connect programme specifically supports several types of activities. Academic Schools This can include: Winter schools. Spring schools. Summer schools. Fall schools. These programmes should have a clear focus on academic development and support for early-career sociologists. Mentoring and Professional Development Events Funding can also support events designed to provide early-career researchers with mentoring, career advice, professional development, and opportunities to build relationships with established academics. Workshops and Retreats The programme may also support: Academic workshops. Research retreats. Structured exchange programmes. Similar academic formats. The key requirement is that the activity has a clear focus on early-career researchers and academic development . How to Apply for Connect Funding The Connect application process is designed to be relatively straightforward. Applicants should submit a single PDF document of no more than two pages . The document should include: A brief description of the proposed event. An explanation of how the event fits the Connect funding format. The target audience. The focus of the event. A rough cost estimate. Applications should be sent by email to: info@kohlifoundation.eu Unlike the Kohli Fellowship, Connect applications can be submitted on an ongoing basis . Applications will continue to be considered until the foundation s annual budget has been exhausted. This means applicants should consider submitting their proposal early rather than assuming funds will remain available throughout the year. Examples of Previously Funded Connect Events The Kohli Foundation has previously supported a number of events through Connect funding. 2025 American Sociological Association Section of Aging and the Life Course The foundation supported a mentoring reception during the American Sociological Association Annual Meeting in Chicago . European Consortium for Sociological Research Funding supported the conference dinner for PhD students at the Annual Conference of the European Consortium for Sociological Research in Cologne. 2024 European Sociological Association The foundation supported a social dinner for PhD students and mentors at the European Sociological Association summer school in Porto. American Sociological Association Section of Aging and the Life Course A mentoring reception during the American Sociological Association Annual Meeting in Montréal was also supported. 2023 The foundation supported a mentoring reception during the American Sociological Association Annual Meeting in Philadelphia , organized through the ASA Section of Aging and the Life Course. These examples demonstrate the range of activities that Connect funding can support, particularly events that create opportunities for mentoring, networking, academic exchange, and professional development. Kohli Foundation Growth Programme Both the Kohli Fellowship and Connect funding form part of the foundation s broader Growth programme. Growth focuses on early-career sociology researchers and seeks to help them develop academically and professionally. The programme supports sociologists who are: Pursuing a PhD. Recently completed a PhD. Developing independent research projects. Building academic networks. Establishing professional profiles. Seeking opportunities to engage with established researchers. The Growth programme therefore addresses different stages of early academic development through both individual fellowship support and event-based funding. Why the Kohli Fellowship Is Valuable for Early-Career Sociologists The fellowship can provide several important benefits to a recently graduated sociologist. Two Years Dedicated to Research The two-year structure provides researchers with substantial time to develop a new research project and advance their academic work. Access to Leading Academic Institutions Fellows are hosted by either WZB in Berlin or EUI in Florence, providing access to established academic communities. Publication Development The fellowship specifically encourages fellows to advance their publications, making it valuable for researchers seeking to strengthen their academic record. Research Collaboration Fellows can develop new research collaborations with scholars at their host institution and beyond. Conferences and Academic Training Researchers have opportunities to participate in academic conferences and training activities, potentially expanding both their knowledge and professional networks. Workshop Organization Fellows can organize their own workshop, providing an opportunity to develop academic leadership and convening experience. Career Development The host institutions provide an environment designed to support the fellow s broader academic and professional development. Why Connect Funding Is Valuable Connect funding provides a different type of support. Rather than funding an individual postdoctoral researcher, it supports academic events that can benefit groups of early-career sociologists. The programme can help create opportunities for: Mentoring. Networking. Research exchange. Professional development. Collaboration. Academic visibility. Engagement with established scholars. This makes the programme particularly relevant to academic organizations, sociology associations, research groups, universities, and other institutions organizing activities for early-career researchers. Key Deadlines and Timelines Applicants should distinguish between the timelines for the two programmes. Kohli Fellowship – WZB Application deadline: Fall 2026 Interviews, selection and notification: Winter 2026/2027 Start date at WZB: 1 October 2027 The exact Fall 2026 application deadline should be confirmed through the official fellowship call and application materials. Kohli Fellowship – EUI Application deadline for the Max Weber Programme: Fall 2027 Interviews, selection and notification: Winter 2027/2028 Start date at EUI: 1 September 2028 Connect Funding There is no fixed application deadline stated for Connect funding. Applications can be submitted on an ongoing basis and will be considered until the annual budget has been exhausted. How Applicants Can Prepare a Strong Kohli Fellowship Application Potential applicants should ensure that their application demonstrates both academic excellence and a strong fit with the fellowship. Important preparation steps include: Update your academic CV and include a complete publication list. Develop a strong research proposal that clearly explains the project you want to pursue. Demonstrate research relevance to the programme of the selected host institution. Prepare a compelling Academic Career Statement explaining your academic trajectory and future goals. Select suitable academic referees who know your research well. Contact referees in advance and confirm their willingness to provide a reference. Review the host institution s research priorities before finalizing your proposal. Clearly explain the contribution of the proposed project to sociology. Demonstrate how the fellowship will advance your research and career. Prepare early , especially for the WZB application timeline in Fall 2026. How Organizations Can Prepare a Strong Connect Proposal Organizations or groups seeking Connect funding should ensure that their proposal clearly demonstrates why the event deserves support. The two-page PDF should clearly explain: What the event is. Who will participate. Why early-career researchers are the target audience. How the event supports academic development. How it promotes networking or mentoring. What participants will gain. How the event connects to independent research or professional development. The estimated cost of organizing the activity. Because applications are considered until the annual budget is exhausted, submitting a well-prepared proposal early may be beneficial. Important Distinction Between the Two Opportunities Although both opportunities fall under the Kohli Foundation s Growth programme, they serve different purposes. Kohli Fellowship The fellowship provides individual postdoctoral research support for an outstanding early-career sociologist. It offers a two-year research placement at WZB or EUI. Connect Funding Connect provides financial support for academic events and structured activities designed to support early-career sociologists. It is intended for activities such as academic schools, mentoring events, workshops, retreats, and similar programmes. Applicants should therefore choose the programme that corresponds to the type of support they are seeking. Conclusion The Kohli Fellowship for Sociology and Connect funding programme provide valuable opportunities for developing the next generation of sociology researchers. The Kohli Fellowship offers exceptional early-career sociologists the opportunity to spend two years conducting research at either WZB in Berlin or the European University Institute in Florence , while developing publications, research collaborations, academic networks, and professional qualifications. The fellowship is open to scholars of all nationalities , provided they meet the doctoral-degree and research requirements. Applicants must have received their PhD no more than five years before the fellowship begins and must have defended their dissertation before the contract starts. Meanwhile, the Connect funding programme supports academic schools, mentoring activities, workshops, retreats, and similar events that promote academic development, professional growth, research advancement, and networking among early-career sociologists. For researchers considering the Kohli Fellowship, the WZB application deadline falls in Fall 2026 , with the successful fellow expected to begin at WZB on 1 October 2027 . The EUI route has a later application timeline, with applications for the Max Weber Programme scheduled for Fall 2027 and the fellowship beginning at EUI on 1 September 2028 . For Connect funding, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis until the annual funding budget has been exhausted. Together, these programmes demonstrate the Kohli Foundation for Sociology s commitment to strengthening early-career academic research, professional networks, collaboration, mentorship, and the long-term development of sociology as a discipline. title: 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant: Fully Funded Fieldwork Support for Master’s and PhD Researchers
summary: Applications are now open for the 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant (YSRG) , an academic research funding opportunity designed to support postgraduate researchers from ASEAN Member States and the Republic of Korea who are pursuing research related to Southeast Asia, ASEAN, and ASEAN-Korea relations. Organized by the Korean Association of Southeast Asian Studies (KASEAS) as part of the ASEAN-Korea Platform for Great Minds (AKPGM) project, the 2026 Young Scholar Research Grant provides selected researchers with financial and academic support to undertake fieldwork that contributes to a deeper understanding of Southeast Asian societies, regional developments, and ASEAN-Korea relations. The AKPGM project is supported by the Government of the Republic of Korea through the ASEAN-Korea Cooperation Fund (AKCF) . Successful applicants can receive round-trip international airfare, a monthly fieldwork stipend of USD 1,400 for up to three months, support for a local research advisor, and participation in an online Young Scholar Research Workshop . Eligible postgraduate researchers interested in conducting locally grounded research in Southeast Asia should carefully review the requirements and prepare their applications before the 5 September 2026 application deadline . About the 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant The ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant (YSRG) is intended to help develop the next generation of scholars specializing in Southeast Asian and ASEAN-related studies. Rather than supporting research that exists only within the classroom or university environment, the program places particular importance on fieldwork and locally grounded research . This approach allows postgraduate researchers to develop their academic work through direct engagement with the societies, institutions, communities, issues, and regional dynamics they are studying. The grant particularly seeks to advance knowledge and academic exchange in areas including: Southeast Asian Studies ASEAN Studies ASEAN-Korea Studies Southeast Asian societies Regional issues affecting Southeast Asia ASEAN-Korea relations Broader political, social, cultural, economic, and regional dynamics relevant to Southeast Asia Through the grant, researchers have an opportunity to strengthen their postgraduate research while contributing to broader academic understanding of Southeast Asia and relations between ASEAN and the Republic of Korea. Financial Benefits of the 2026 Young Scholar Research Grant One of the major features of the ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant is the financial support available for approved fieldwork. Selected grantees will receive the following benefits: 1. Round-Trip International Airfare The program provides round-trip international airfare for approved fieldwork . This support can significantly reduce one of the major financial barriers facing postgraduate students who need to travel internationally to conduct research. Applicants should ensure that their proposed fieldwork destination and activities are clearly connected to their research objectives. 2. USD 1,400 Monthly Fieldwork Stipend Selected researchers will receive a monthly fieldwork stipend of USD 1,400 for up to three months . For a grantee receiving the stipend for the maximum three-month period, this represents up to USD 4,200 in fieldwork stipend support . The duration of support will depend on the approved fieldwork arrangements under the program. 3. USD 200 Honorarium for Local Research Advisors The program also provides an honorarium of USD 200 for local research advisors . Having access to locally knowledgeable academic or research support can be particularly valuable for international fieldwork. Local advisors may help researchers better understand the academic, institutional, cultural, or practical context surrounding their research. 4. Young Scholar Research Workshop Selected grantees will also participate in the Young Scholar Research Workshop , which will be conducted online. This academic component complements the financial support offered by the grant and provides an opportunity for young scholars to participate in research-oriented academic exchange. Who Can Apply for the 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant? Applicants must satisfy several nationality, enrollment, and research requirements. Nationality Requirement Applicants must be nationals of an ASEAN Member State or the Republic of Korea . This means the program is specifically targeted toward postgraduate researchers from ASEAN countries and South Korea rather than being an unrestricted global research grant. Academic Enrollment Requirement Applicants must currently be enrolled in either: A Master’s degree programme , or A doctoral programme The programme must be at a recognized institution located in ASEAN or the Republic of Korea . Applicants should therefore note that simply holding an undergraduate degree or having an interest in Southeast Asian Studies is not sufficient. The opportunity specifically targets postgraduate researchers who are currently pursuing Master s or doctoral studies. A Certificate of Enrollment is among the documents required as part of the application. Eligible Areas of Research Proposed research must be relevant to one or more of the following broad academic areas: Southeast Asian Studies ASEAN Studies ASEAN-Korea Studies Research concerning Southeast Asian societies Regional issues involving Southeast Asia ASEAN-Korea relations The program is therefore suitable for postgraduate researchers whose work contributes meaningfully to understanding Southeast Asia and its broader regional relationships. Applicants should ensure that their research proposal clearly explains how the project contributes to one or more of these fields. Simply mentioning Southeast Asia without demonstrating a meaningful academic connection may not be sufficient, particularly because the relevance of the proposed research is one of the stated evaluation criteria. Regional Representation in the Selection Process The program seeks to encourage balanced regional representation . According to the grant guidelines, the selection committee generally aims to award up to one grant per ASEAN Member State and the Republic of Korea . However, this should not be interpreted as an automatic allocation of one grant to every eligible country. Awards remain subject to the quality of applications received . Applicants will therefore still need to submit academically strong, original, relevant, and feasible research proposals. Selection Priorities Applicants Should Understand Meeting the basic eligibility criteria does not necessarily mean that every eligible proposal will receive equal priority. The program has identified several selection priorities that applicants should carefully consider when developing their applications. Priority for Applicants Studying in Their Home Countries Priority will be given to applicants who are enrolled at institutions in their home countries . This does not necessarily mean that eligible students studying elsewhere within ASEAN or the Republic of Korea cannot apply. Rather, institutional affiliation in the applicant s home country is specifically identified as a selection priority. Applicants should distinguish between eligibility requirements and selection priorities when assessing their chances. Research Beyond the Applicant s Own National Context Is Encouraged Applications can propose research concerning any country or region in Southeast Asia . However, an important objective of the grant is to encourage Southeast Asian Studies as the study of Southeast Asia beyond an applicant s own national setting. Consequently, lower priority may be given to proposals that focus exclusively on the applicant s home country or on the country where the applicant is currently enrolled . For example, a researcher may strengthen the regional dimension of a proposal by examining: Cross-border developments Comparative Southeast Asian issues Regional institutions ASEAN cooperation Relationships between different Southeast Asian societies ASEAN-Korea relations Regional political, social, economic, or cultural dynamics Applicants should not artificially broaden a research topic merely to satisfy this priority. Instead, where academically appropriate, proposals should demonstrate how the research contributes to a wider understanding of Southeast Asia. Are STEM Research Proposals Eligible? Applicants from Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics disciplines should pay particular attention to the program s research scope. The Young Scholar Research Grant is primarily intended to support Southeast Asian Studies and related area studies research . Therefore, proposals that are primarily: Technical, Laboratory-based, or Exclusively focused on Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics are not eligible under the normal scope of the grant. There is, however, a limited interdisciplinary exception. A STEM-related research project may potentially be considered when it demonstrates strong interdisciplinary engagement with the social sciences or humanities and makes a clear contribution to understanding Southeast Asia or ASEAN-Korea relations . Applicants proposing interdisciplinary research should make this connection explicit and substantive in their research proposal. How Applications Will Be Evaluated Applications for the 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant will be assessed according to several important criteria. Understanding these criteria can help applicants prepare stronger research proposals. 1. Academic Quality, Originality and Significance The proposed research should demonstrate strong academic quality. Applicants should clearly communicate: What they intend to investigate Why the research question is important What gap or issue the research addresses How the project contributes to existing knowledge What makes the proposed research original Why the findings could be academically significant 2. Relevance to Southeast Asian, ASEAN or ASEAN-Korea Studies Applicants need to demonstrate a clear connection between their proposed research and the program s academic objectives. Relevant projects should contribute to: Southeast Asian Studies, ASEAN Studies, or ASEAN-Korea Studies. The relationship between the proposed fieldwork and these areas should be clearly established within the research proposal. 3. Quality and Feasibility of the Proposed Fieldwork A strong research idea must also be practical. The selection process will consider whether the proposed fieldwork can realistically be completed within the available period and whether the planned activities are appropriate for answering the research questions. Applicants should therefore develop a fieldwork plan that is focused, achievable, and logically connected to their research methodology. 4. Research Capacity and Preparedness The applicant s own research capacity and level of preparation will also be assessed. This makes the overall quality of the application important. The research proposal, CV, academic history, enrollment information, and other supporting documents should collectively demonstrate that the applicant is adequately prepared to conduct the proposed research. Required Application Documents Applicants must prepare and upload several documents as part of the application. The required documents are: Research Proposal Host Institution Introduction (Fieldwork Site) Curriculum Vitae (CV) Certificate of Enrollment from the current or most recent academic institution Academic Transcript, including records up to the most recent semester Applicants should prepare these materials carefully and ensure that all information is accurate and consistent across the application. Research Proposal The research proposal is likely to be one of the most important components because the evaluation criteria place considerable emphasis on academic quality, originality, significance, relevance, feasibility, and research preparedness. Applicants should ensure their proposal clearly communicates the research problem, objectives, significance, methodology, fieldwork plan, and relevance to the grant s focus. Host Institution Introduction Applicants are also required to submit information introducing the host institution associated with the fieldwork site . Applicants should follow the official application form and any accompanying instructions when preparing this requirement. Curriculum Vitae The CV should provide an organized overview of the applicant s academic and relevant research background. Applicants should ensure that the information presented is current at the time of application. Certificate of Enrollment A Certificate of Enrollment is required to establish the applicant s academic status. Because applicants must be currently enrolled in a Master s or doctoral programme at a recognized institution in ASEAN or the Republic of Korea, this document is particularly important for demonstrating eligibility. Academic Transcript Applicants must also provide an academic transcript containing records through the most recent semester . Applicants should make sure that the submitted transcript is sufficiently current and meets any specifications provided through the official application system. How to Apply for the 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant Applications must be submitted through the program s official online application form . Applicants should complete the online form and upload the required supporting documents as instructed. Before submitting an application, candidates should: Confirm that they satisfy the nationality requirements. Confirm that they are currently enrolled in an eligible Master s or doctoral programme. Ensure that their proposed research falls within an eligible research area. Review the program s research and institutional selection priorities. Prepare a strong and feasible research proposal. Prepare the host institution introduction. Update their CV. Obtain their Certificate of Enrollment. Obtain an academic transcript covering the most recent semester. Review all application materials for accuracy and completeness. Submit the complete application through the official online application form before the deadline. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to prepare or upload their documents, particularly if official academic records need to be obtained from their university. APPLY NOW 2026 ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant Deadline The application deadline is 5 September 2026 . Applications and all required documents should be completed and submitted through the official application system by the stated deadline. Applicants should pay particular attention to this date because incomplete or late applications may not receive consideration under the selection process. Important Dates and Timeline The announced schedule for the 2026 program is as follows: Application Deadline: 5 September 2026 Results Announcement: Fourth week of October 2026 Orientation: Second week of November 2026 Fieldwork Period: Late November 2026 to April 2027 Applicants who are selected should therefore be prepared for orientation in November and for approved fieldwork to take place during the period extending from late November 2026 through April 2027. Why Postgraduate Researchers Should Consider This Opportunity Fieldwork can be one of the most valuable components of postgraduate research, but it can also be financially difficult to undertake, particularly when international travel is required. The ASEAN-Korea Young Scholar Research Grant addresses several of these barriers by combining financial support with academic engagement. The opportunity is particularly significant because it provides: International airfare for approved fieldwork A substantial monthly fieldwork stipend Support for engagement with a local research advisor An academic workshop Opportunities for locally grounded research Support for emerging Southeast Asianists An emphasis on regional and cross-national research Opportunities to strengthen understanding of ASEAN-Korea relations For Master s and doctoral researchers whose projects require field-based investigation in Southeast Asia, these benefits can provide valuable support for developing more rigorous and regionally informed research. title: UN Global Compact SPARK 2026: Practical Sustainability Training for SMEs and Suppliers to Strengthen Global Competitiveness
summary: Sustainability is becoming an increasingly important part of doing business. Companies of all sizes are facing growing expectations from customers, investors, business partners, regulators and global supply chains to understand and manage their environmental, social and governance impacts. For small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and suppliers, meeting these expectations can sometimes feel complicated, especially when businesses have limited time, staff and financial resources. The United Nations Global Compact SPARK programme is designed to make this process more manageable. SPARK is a structured, practical learning journey that helps SMEs and suppliers develop the knowledge, tools and capabilities they need to strengthen their sustainability practices and respond to changing expectations across global value chains. The 2026 SPARK programme has been streamlined into a focused three-month learning journey running from 10 September to 10 December 2026 . The programme is designed to reduce the time burden on participating businesses while providing clear milestones and practical resources that can be applied directly to day-to-day operations. Rather than expecting businesses to solve every sustainability issue at once, SPARK focuses on helping participants understand where to start, identify priorities and develop a practical plan for improvement. What Is the UN Global Compact SPARK Programme? SPARK is the United Nations Global Compact s global learning programme for SMEs and suppliers . It has been developed to provide businesses with practical guidance, tools and resources that can help them strengthen their sustainability practices. The programme recognises that many SMEs and suppliers are increasingly expected to demonstrate responsible business practices but may not have the same resources as large multinational corporations. SPARK therefore takes a practical and accessible approach. Instead of overwhelming businesses with complex sustainability frameworks, the programme provides a structured learning journey that helps participants progressively understand sustainability expectations and translate that knowledge into action. The programme is particularly relevant to businesses that are: Beginning their sustainability journey Trying to understand what sustainability means for their operations Responding to sustainability requirements from customers Working with larger companies or multinational supply chains Seeking to strengthen existing sustainability practices Preparing for changing regulatory or market expectations Looking to improve their position within global value chains Why Sustainability Matters for SMEs and Suppliers Sustainability is no longer an issue that concerns only large corporations. Businesses throughout global supply chains are increasingly being asked to provide information about how they manage environmental, social and governance issues. For suppliers and SMEs, this can affect their ability to: Win new customers Maintain relationships with existing customers Participate in international supply chains Meet procurement requirements Demonstrate responsible business practices Respond to regulatory expectations Build credibility with business partners Remain competitive in changing markets Large companies increasingly need information from their suppliers about sustainability performance, creating a growing need for SMEs to understand and manage their own environmental and social impacts. SPARK is designed to help businesses respond to these changing expectations without requiring them to undertake everything simultaneously. The Core Philosophy Behind SPARK A central idea of SPARK is that businesses do not need to solve every sustainability challenge immediately. Instead, businesses need to develop: A clear understanding of sustainability expectations. An understanding of their most important risks and impacts. A set of realistic priorities. A practical plan for improvement. The ability to implement that plan within their operations. This step-by-step approach can make sustainability more manageable for businesses that are working with limited resources. Rather than treating sustainability as a separate theoretical exercise, SPARK encourages participants to connect sustainability learning with their everyday business activities. What Businesses Can Learn Through SPARK Participating businesses can develop a stronger understanding of sustainability across environmental, social and governance (ESG) areas. The programme is designed to help participants gain clarity about what sustainability expectations mean for their businesses and how they can begin responding to them. Environmental Sustainability Environmental issues are increasingly important across global value chains. Through the programme, businesses can develop greater awareness of environmental sustainability expectations and consider how these issues relate to their own operations. This can help businesses think more systematically about their environmental impacts and identify areas where improvements may be appropriate. Social Sustainability Social sustainability focuses on the people affected by business activities. For SMEs and suppliers, social considerations can be relevant to areas such as responsible employment practices, workers, communities and relationships throughout supply chains. Understanding these issues can help businesses build more responsible and resilient operations. Governance Good governance is an important component of responsible business. Businesses need appropriate structures and processes for identifying risks, making decisions and demonstrating accountability. SPARK introduces participants to sustainability expectations across these areas and helps them understand how they can begin integrating sustainability considerations into their business approach. Why Join SPARK 2026? There are several potential benefits for businesses participating in the programme. 1. Gain Clarity on Sustainability Expectations Sustainability can involve a wide range of issues, frameworks and expectations. SPARK helps businesses develop a clearer understanding of what is expected across environmental, social and governance areas. This can make it easier for business leaders and teams to determine where to focus their attention. 2. Identify Risks and Priorities Businesses cannot necessarily address every sustainability issue at once. SPARK helps participants learn how to identify relevant risks and determine which areas should receive priority. This can help businesses move from general awareness to practical decision-making. 3. Develop Practical Improvements The programme is designed around implementation. Participants are not simply introduced to sustainability concepts. They are provided with tools and resources that can support the process of applying their learning within their own businesses. This practical focus is particularly relevant for SMEs and suppliers that need solutions that can work within their existing operational constraints. 4. Strengthen Business Credibility Demonstrating an understanding of sustainability can help businesses strengthen their credibility with customers, partners and other stakeholders. For suppliers in particular, stronger sustainability capabilities can help them respond to increasing expectations from companies further up the value chain. 5. Improve Positioning Within Global Value Chains Businesses participating in international or multinational supply chains may increasingly encounter sustainability requirements. Developing sustainability knowledge and capabilities can help SMEs and suppliers better understand and respond to these expectations. SPARK is therefore relevant not only from a sustainability perspective but also from a business competitiveness perspective . 6. Learn From Experts The programme includes live sessions involving subject matter and business experts. Connect With Other Businesses Participants can also learn from other businesses facing similar sustainability challenges. The programme is designed to help businesses gradually develop their sustainability capabilities instead of attempting to address every issue at once. The learning journey can help participants move through several broad stages: Stage 1: Understand The first step is developing an understanding of sustainability and the expectations businesses increasingly face. This provides the foundation for identifying what sustainability means within a particular business context. Stage 2: Identify Businesses can then consider their sustainability risks, impacts and areas requiring attention. This stage helps participants move beyond general awareness and consider their own operations. Stage 3: Prioritise Not every issue will have the same level of importance or urgency. Participants can learn how to determine which areas should be prioritised based on their business circumstances and sustainability risks. Stage 4: Plan Once priorities have been identified, businesses can begin developing a practical approach to addressing them.
